To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the formation of polyeletrolyte complexes between PLGA microspherical surfaces and nanoparticles results in the creation of stable 2D assemblies that can be used as cell delivery vehicles and (ii) these assemblies can be used to create 3D scaffolding structures that can serve as cell delivery vehicles.
the use of heparin/pL-lysine nanoparticles results in the formation of a 3D nanostructured surface on a microsphere, which is an excellent structure for the delivery of cells.
the use of heparin/polyl-lysine NPs on PLGA microspherical surfaces results in an excellent 3D scaffold for stem cell delivery.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a simple, efficient, and highly versatile method for the complete encapsulation of various NPs within microspheres.
the design and development of novel 3D nanostructures that are stabilized via embedment in PLGA microspherical structures.
the design and fabrication of a 3D microspherical structure that is coated with various NPs for use as a cell delivery vehicle.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the results of this study demonstrate that the use of heparin/polyllysine NPs to coat the PLGA microsphere surface is a simple and efficient method for the stabilization of 2D assemblies and that the resulting structures are excellent cell delivery vehicles.
this study demonstrated the possibility of the use of PLGAmicrosphere surface-coating with heparin and polylysine NPs to create an efficient cell delivery vehicle.
this study demonstrates the feasibility of a novel approach for the preparation of 2D nanostructured films via the use of PLGAmicrospheres.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the heparin/p(L-lysine)-PLGA microsphere system is a promising candidate for the construction of a 3D cell delivery vehicle.

we have developed a novel method for the fabrication of polyelectrollyte complex microspheres that are capable of being used in a variety of biomedical applications, including cell encapsulation and tissue engineering.

the use of a simple and efficient method for the stabilization of 3D nanostructures via embedment into a spherical microstructure is a promising approach for the fabrication of 3D scaffolding materials.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the use of a PLGA microspherical structure as a scaffold is an efficient method for stabilizing the 2D assemblies formed by electrostatic interactions, and this method may be used to construct various types of 2D assemblies.
the use of polyelectrollytes as a coating for PLGA microspherical structures results in a stable structure.
the use of heparin/p(Lys) NPs as the coating material on the surface of PLGA microspherical scaffolds is an efficient and simple approach to the stabilization of 3D assemblies of various NPs.
